standard.title: Rounding and Estimation
standard.description: round decimals to a given accuracy appropriate to the context and use appropriate rounding and estimation to check the reasonableness of solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can round whole numbers and simple decimals. Students understand decimal place value and can multiply/divide decimals by powers of 10 (from AC9M6N04, AC9M6N06).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students round decimals to a specified accuracy appropriate to the context and use estimation to judge whether solutions are reasonable.

nodes.label: Rounding decimals to specified places
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students round decimals to a given number of decimal places using standard rounding conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Round a decimal to 1, 2 or 3 decimal places as specified.
nodes.typical_width: Round to specified decimal places across a range of contexts; explain the rounding rule and why the convention exists.
wider: Investigate contexts where rounding up or rounding down is more appropriate than standard rounding (e.g. buying enough paint — always round up).
Explore the effect of rounding at each step of a multi-step calculation vs rounding only at the end.

response_modes.reason: Students who only practise decontextualised rounding often fail to select appropriate accuracy in context. Varied practical contexts are needed to build judgment about what 'appropriate' means.

success_criteria: Correctly rounds a decimal to a specified number of decimal places.
Applies the 'round half up' convention consistently.
Does not confuse rounding to 2 decimal places with rounding to the nearest 100.

nodes.label: Context-appropriate accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students choose an appropriate level of rounding for a given context and explain why that accuracy is suitable.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a practical problem (e.g. measuring fabric, calculating cost), state appropriate rounding and justify the choice.
nodes.typical_width: Compare the effect of different levels of rounding across several contexts and evaluate which is most appropriate for each.
wider: Investigate situations where over-precision misleads (e.g. reporting a population estimate to the nearest unit).
Discuss how measurement accuracy relates to rounding: a ruler accurate to 1mm supports reporting to 1dp in cm.

response_modes.reason: Judging appropriate accuracy requires a reasoning process students rarely apply spontaneously: What is the purpose of the answer? What precision is the measurement tool capable of? Does the context require over- or under-estimation?

success_criteria: Selects a contextually appropriate level of decimal accuracy and justifies it.
Recognises that different contexts require different precision.
Can explain why rounding to too many places can give a false sense of precision.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Reasoning about appropriate precision and the misleading effects of over-precision connects mathematics to real-world decision-making — advancing students can engage with this as a genuine critical thinking task.

nodes.label: Estimation to check reasonableness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students use estimation strategies (front-end, rounding, compatible numbers) to check whether a calculated solution is reasonable.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate the answer to a calculation and compare with the computed result to check reasonableness.
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple estimation strategies; identify when a computed answer is unreasonable and diagnose the likely error.
wider: Use estimation as a first step in multi-step problems to set bounds on the expected answer before computing.
Investigate how a calculator error (e.g. missing a decimal point) is caught by estimation.

response_modes.reason: Estimation as a reasonableness check only becomes habitual across a wide variety of problem types. Students who practise estimation only in drill exercises rarely apply it spontaneously in problem-solving.

success_criteria: Produces a reasonable estimate before or after computing.
Identifies whether a given answer is unreasonable based on estimation.
